intro.title: Build background job queue with retries
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple background job queue system in Node.js that can process tasks asynchronously, outside of your main application flow. You'll learn how to implement retry logic, which automatically re-attempts failed jobs a set number of times before marking them as permanently failed. The core programming concepts involved are asynchronous programming, event-driven architecture, and error handling. You'll use key Node.js constructs like Promises, setTimeout for delays, and basic data structures to manage the job queue. By the end, you'll have a foundational understanding of how background processing and resilience patterns work in server-side applications.
intro.usecase: Background job queues with retries are essential in production applications where reliability matters. When you upload a profile picture on social media, the platform uses a job queue to resize and optimize your image in the background while keeping the UI responsive. E-commerce sites queue order confirmation emails and inventory updates, ensuring they retry if the email service is temporarily down. This pattern prevents user-facing delays and handles failures gracefully in real-world systems.
